name: Non-terminal Myelocystocele

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-terminal Myelocystocele

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic mass along the dorsal midline of the spinal cord without terminal location
Identification of a dilated central canal (hydromyelia) forming a cystic cavity within the spinal cord on imaging
Lack of a terminal sac or lipoma at the distal end of the spinal cord differentiating from terminal myelocystocele
Presence of neurological signs such as lower limb weakness or sensory deficits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cystic dorsal spinal mass with hydromyelic cyst on imaging and absence of terminal sac
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on clinical examination and MRI findings differentiating from terminal myelocystocele and other spinal dysraphisms.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible or palpable cystic swelling along the back

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hydromyelia with cystic dilation of central canal

common.notes: Including decreased pain and temperature sensation
searchTerms: sensory loss in feet and legs
increased muscle tone in lower limbs

occasional.notes: Skin dimples, tufts of hair, or hemangiomas
searchTerms: skin signs on back over spine problem

occasional.notes: Congenital deformities associated with spinal dysraphism

rare.notes: Secondary to associated neural tube defects
Due to cyst rupture or infection
searchTerms: open skin wound on cyst area

imaging: MRI demonstrating cystic dilation of the central canal (hydromyelia) within the spinal cord
Absence of terminal sac or lipoma differentiating from terminal myelocystocele
Visualization of dorsal midline spinal cystic mass
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
Possible association with neural tube defect gene variants
other: Neurological examination revealing lower limb weakness and sensory deficits
Urodynamic studies confirming neurogenic bladder dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of terminal sac or lipoma at distal spinal cord
Location of cyst at terminal end of spinal cord
Open spinal defect with exposed neural tissue
Characteristic sac containing meninges and spinal cord
Cystic mass containing only meninges without neural tissue
No hydromyelia or central canal dilation

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of spinal cystic mass
Signs of infection or ulceration over cyst
Progressive neurological deterioration including worsening weakness or bladder dysfunction
